title: Cokret Cursor
description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'after', 'before', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Cokret-Wait-For'). Wire form is always ck:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §10): v1 core uses the stateful opaque-handle form only — body is {v, purpose, t, x, h} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) tuple. Server-side handle lookup IS the integrity check; there is no inline transcript binding to verify on the client side. Servers MUST reject unknown / expired / cross-binding handles with cursor_integrity_invalid.

Stateless self-describing cursors (MAC- or signature-bound inline body with positions, target and issuer_kid) are NOT part of the v1 core schema. Implementations that need a stateless cursor MUST opt in to the ck.profile.stateless_cursor.v1 profile, which extends this schema with the inline body fields and integrity proof. Core consumers (sync, federation, snapshot) do not need to implement the stateless path.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'after' on /account/subscribe, 'before' / 'after' on ck.self.events.query and ck.peer.events.query (including its service-to-service federation pull form GET /_cokret/peer/events?before=<cursor>), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Cokret-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). The handle binding (resolved server-side) carries positions for 'stream' or target for 'barrier'; the wire body does not.

x.description: Expiration timestamp (Unix ms). MUST be in the future when the cursor is issued. TTL upper bounds (cursor lifetime = x - t_ms): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days). Issuing a cursor exceeding these caps is a producer error; receivers MUST reject with `invalid_param`. Reasoning: barrier cursors only gate read-your-writes wait latency and become meaningless once the global frontier has long covered the target event. Stream cursors lose causal alignment value over weeks of activity.

h.description: Server-side opaque handle. The issuing server MUST bind this handle to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) and MUST be able to revoke it. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding); minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically (base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet). Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. Handle lookup IS the integrity check — there is no MAC or signature to verify inline. This is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. Servers SHOULD keep the handle → binding map durable across process restarts (see client-sync.md §12.1): a memory-only table is still integrity-correct (unknown handles fail closed) but turns every restart into a fleet-wide forced full resync. For production-grade deployment profiles (small_team / organization / high_security_organization / sovereign_deployment / sovereign_enclave / isolated_sovereign_network) this durability plus TTL GC is a MUST per client-sync.md §12.1; only personal_node keeps it at SHOULD.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore. Auxiliary `_*` fields are excluded from cursor migration translation. In v1 core (stateful-only) there is no `_mac` / `_sig` integrity field — handle lookup IS the integrity check — so the underscore namespace is fully private to the issuing server. `_mac` and `_sig` themselves are explicitly excluded by the top-level `not` clause: a core body carrying either MUST be rejected (encoding.md §8.3 rule 13); they are only meaningful under the ck.profile.stateless_cursor.v1 overlay schema.
